# Biological Interpretation of the PTMA→Ki-67 Decision-Tree Logic in Breast Cancer

## 0. Reading frame: what the tree is actually classifying

The Class 1 label marks the **top 10% of positive IG attribution** — i.e., samples where PTMA expression *pushes the model's Ki-67 prediction upward most strongly*. The tree therefore answers: **under which molecular contexts does PTMA become tightly and positively coupled to Ki-67?**

The full tree (supplementary) uses only a compact, functionally coherent feature set, which I group into three modules:

| Module | Features in the tree | Cellular function |
|---|---|---|
| RNA processing / mRNA maturation | **HNRNPA2B1**, **PABPC1** | Splicing, m6A-dependent RNA processing, mRNA stability & poly(A)-dependent initiation |
| Translation / ribosome biogenesis | **RPLP0**, RPL21, RPS27, **PABPC1** | Ribosomal stalk, protein-synthesis capacity, nucleolar output |
| Mitotic microtubule apparatus | **TUBB4B**, **TUBA1C** | α/β-tubulin isotypes, spindle assembly, mitotic commitment |

Two architectural facts drive the interpretation:

1. **HNRNPA2B1 is the root split** — the RNA-processing state is the single most decisive determinant of whether PTMA positively informs Ki-67.
2. **Compensation logic**: whenever one module is weak, the tree demands *stronger or alternative* signals from the others (e.g., when HNRNPA2B1 ≤ 0.333, Class 1 requires RPLP0 > 0.444 — a much higher threshold — plus TUBB4B > –0.194 and TUBA1C > 0.588, Node 16; note that "TUBB4B > –0.194" merely means "not suppressed"). This is a modular **AND-gate with partial redundancy**, not a single-gene effect.

---

## ZONE 1 (PRIMARY HIGHLIGHT): Node 14 — *HNRNPA2B1 > 0.333 & TUBB4B > 0.489 & RPLP0 > 0.169*

### Why this zone is the most robust
- **TP = 1,147**, the largest capture of any leaf; with all four Class-1 leaves summing to 1,843 TP, Node 14 alone contains **~62% of all high-attribution samples**.
- **Precision = 51.4%** — the highest of all leaves — and **Gini = 0.3095**, the most homogeneous leaf in the tree.
- The rule is only **depth-3** (three conditions), making it the most generalizable logic. Node 13 (the sibling leaf, identical except RPLP0 ≤ 0.169) has precision of only 23.8% (Gini ≈ 0.49): kept as Class 1 only because `class_weight={0:1, 1:4}` biases the tree toward recall. The RPLP0 sub-split therefore functions as a **purity-refinement operator that more than doubles precision (23.8% → 51.4%)** — this contrast is itself biologically informative (see H2 below).

### Rule → biology mapping

| Condition | Interpretation |
|---|---|
| HNRNPA2B1 > 0.333 | Tumor runs a **high-amplitude RNA-processing program**: hnRNP A2/B1 is an oncofetal splicing/RNA-processing factor overexpressed in aggressive breast cancer; high expression implies massive pre-mRNA flux requiring processing (incl. alternatively spliced proliferative isoforms) |
| TUBB4B > 0.489 | **Mitotic commitment**: β-tubulin isotype expansion = active spindle program, cells traversing S/G2/M |
| RPLP0 > 0.169 | **Translation floor**: ribosomal stalk protein P0 above baseline = ribosome biogenesis/protein output sufficient to sustain production of abundant proliferation proteins |

### Integrative mechanism narrative ("how PTMA and the co-factors jointly determine Ki-67")

The node describes a **three-gates-open state**, and this is precisely where PTMA is maximally informative about Ki-67. The proposed circuit:

**Oncogenic transcriptional drive (Myc/E2F) → co-induces PTMA, MKI67, HNRNPA2B1, ribosomal genes, PABPC1, tubulins → PTMA executes a chromatin "gate-opening" step (histone H1 displacement, transcriptional coactivation) that sustains high-amplitude transcription of the program, including MKI67 → the transcript wave is processed by hnRNP A2/B1, stabilized/translated by the PABP–ribosome axis, and executed by the tubulin spindle.**

PTMA and Ki-67 are thus **two effectors of the same upstream proliferation program** — PTMA being the chromatin-permissive node, Ki-67 the chromatin-output marker (and itself a chromatin/nucleolus-associated protein involved in heterochromatin and rRNA regulation). When RNA processing, translation, and mitotic modules are all engaged, PTMA's expression level becomes the highest-fidelity single proxy for the whole program — which is exactly why the nonlinear model loads heavy positive attribution onto PTMA in these samples. When a module is missing, PTMA alone becomes an ambiguous cue (high FP), and Ki-67 must be explained by other features.

### Category 1 — Findings that directly confirm existing literature

1. **PTMA is a proliferation-linked, Myc-responsive nuclear protein with histone-chaperone/coactivator activity** — its strong positive attribution to Ki-67 in proliferative contexts is the expected behavior of a gene whose expression rises with mitogenic stimulation and supports transcription of growth-program genes (Karetsou et al. 1998; Coller et al. 2000; Dang et al. 2006).
2. **Ki-67 (MKI67) is the canonical proliferation readout in breast cancer**, used clinically to define high-proliferative phenotypes (Scholzen & Gerdes 2000; Yerushalmi et al. 2010; Coates et al. 2015). Recovering the PTMA–Ki-67 axis inside a proliferation-gene network confirms known biology rather than an artifact.
3. **Co-activation of splicing, ribosomal, and tubulin genes with MKI67 reproduces the established tumor "proliferation signature"** — genes periodically expressed in the cell cycle are co-upregulated in tumors (Whitfield et al. 2002; Ruggero & Pandolfi 2003; Dumontet & Jordan 2010).
4. **HNRNPA2B1 as root gate is consistent with its documented role in aggressive breast cancer RNA-processing programs** (Alarcón et al. 2015; David & Manley 2010).
5. **The RPLP0 and Ki-67 positions confirm a chromatin–nucleolar axis**: Ki-67 itself participates in heterochromatin/rRNA regulation (Sun & Kaufman 2018), placing PTMA (chromatin/H1), Ki-67 (chromosome periphery/nucleolus), and RPLP0 (ribosome) on one coherent functional axis.

### Category 2 — Novel, testable mechanisms (literature-supported)

**H1. Conditional chromatin-coactivator model (splicing-gated PTMA→MKI67 transcription).** The root gate predicts PTMA's H1-displacement/chromatin-opening activity supports MKI67 transcription *only when RNA processing and translation are concurrently active*.
*Test:* PTMA knockdown (siRNA/CRISPRi) ± HNRNPA2B1 knockdown in Zone-14-like lines (high-mitotic-index basal models, e.g., MDA-MB-231/HCC1937); read out MKI67 nascent transcription (4sU-qPCR), Ki-67 protein (IHC/Western), and chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq/MNase). *Prediction:* PTMA loss collapses MKI67 transcription and opens H1-condensed chromatin; the effect is attenuated in HNRNPA2B1-low cells (matching Node 16's compensatory higher thresholds).

**H2. Translation-capacity "fidelity gate" on the PTMA–Ki-67 axis (Node 13 vs 14 contrast).** The RPLP0 floor (0.169) doubling precision suggests ribosome output is required to keep Ki-67 protein coherent with PTMA-driven transcription.
*Test:* Ribosome-biogenesis stress (RPLP0 siRNA; Pol I inhibition, e.g., CX-5461) in Zone-14-mimicking cells. *Prediction:* Ki-67 **protein** falls faster than MKI67 mRNA, and PTMA–Ki-67 protein correlation decouples — mechanistically explaining Node 13's false-positive-rich profile (splicing + mitotic signals on, translation insufficient → markers decohere).

**H3. PTMA–Ki-67 physical association at the mitotic chromosome periphery.** PTMA is a highly acidic intrinsically disordered protein with documented affinity for basic nucleosome-associated partners (histone H1); Ki-67 is a basic, chromatin-coating proliferation protein. The tree's dependence on mitotic-module genes invites a direct-interaction hypothesis.
*Test:* Co-IP / proximity ligation assay in synchronized mitotic breast cancer cells; PTMA acidic-domain mutants. *Prediction:* PTMA associates with Ki-67's basic repeat region, enriched during G2/M — a mechanism that would explain why attribution peaks in tubulin-high zones. *(Speculative but literature-grounded.)*

**H4. Zone signature as a clinical gate for PTMA's biomarker utility and therapy sensitivity.**
*Test:* In TCGA-BRCA/METABRIC, compute PTMA–MKI67 partial correlation stratified by the three-gate signature; regress MKI67 ~ PTMA × module score. *Prediction:* significantly higher PTMA–MKI67 coupling in Zone-14-positive tumors; Zone-14-positive tumors show enhanced sensitivity to Myc-program collapse (BET inhibitors, e.g., JQ1; Filippakopoulos et al. 2010; Lovén et al. 2013), Pol I/nucleolar stress (Pelletier et al. 2018), and taxanes (Dumontet & Jordan 2010).

---

## ZONE 2 (SECOND HIGHLIGHT): Node 22 — *HNRNPA2B1 > 0.333 & TUBB4B ≤ 0.489 & PABPC1 > 0.645 & TUBA1C > 0.588*

### Why this is the second-most robust zone
- **TP = 268** (second largest) and **Precision = 38.8%** (second highest), Gini 0.41.
- It is the **most specific (depth-4) rule** in the tree: when the β-tubulin arm is off, high PTMA attribution requires the *joint* satisfaction of PABPC1 AND TUBA1C — neither alone suffices. This AND-logic is the key mechanistic signal.

### Integrative mechanism narrative

This zone shares the same root gate (RNA-processing state, HNRNPA2B1 > 0.333) but describes a **compensation state**: the β-tubulin cue is muted, yet PTMA still carries strong Ki-67 information — but only if (i) the poly(A)-dependent translation machinery is amplified (PABPC1 > 0.645) and (ii) the mitotic apparatus remains engaged through the **α-isotype** (TUBA1C > 0.588). Two mechanistic implications:

1. **Spindle-isotype redundancy:** TUBA1C can substitute for TUBB4B as the "division-machinery-on" readout. Microtubules obligately form α/β heterodimers, so either isotype's induction reports spindle load — the tree accepts either arm.
2. **Post-transcriptional sustainment of Ki-67:** when the mitotic β-tubulin signal is weak (plausibly G1/S-skewed, or a less mitotic tumor subset), the PTMA→Ki-67 coupling is maintained through **mRNA stabilization and closed-loop translation initiation** (PABPC1/eIF4G axis) rather than through maximal mitotic transcription. This implies the PTMA–Ki-67 relationship is not merely a co-accumulation artifact of mitosis: PTMA's chromatin-level contribution to Ki-67 persists via the transcription/RNA-metabolism route when translation throughput is high.

### Category 1 — Findings that directly confirm existing literature

1. The shared **HNRNPA2B1 root gate** again confirms the known requirement for high RNA-processing activity in aggressive/proliferative breast tumors (Alarcón et al. 2015; David & Manley 2010).
2. **PABPC1's documented functions in mRNA stabilization and translation initiation** (Kahvejian et al. 2005), and translational reprogramming as a cancer hallmark required for proliferation-protein output (Silvera et al. 2010) — its selection as the compensatory node is exactly what the translation-control literature predicts.
3. **Tubulins are periodically expressed and upregulated with proliferation**; mitotic spindle integrity is a core cancer-therapy target (Whitfield et al. 2002; Dumontet & Jordan 2010) — confirming the necessity of a spindle gate even in the TUBB4B-low branch.

### Category 2 — Novel, testable mechanisms (literature-supported)

**H5. Post-transcriptional sustainment model.** In TUBB4B-low backgrounds, PABPC1 maintains MKI67 mRNA half-life/polysome loading and thus Ki-67 protein.
*Test:* PABPC1 knockdown in TUBB4B-low vs TUBB4B-high breast cancer lines; MKI67 mRNA decay (actinomycin D chase), polysome profiling, PABPC1 CLIP for the MKI67 3′UTR. *Prediction:* Ki-67 protein falls in TUBB4B-low cells disproportionately; in TUBB4B-high cells the transcriptional/mitotic dominance buffers the loss — reproducing the tree's zone separation.

**H6. Spindle-isotype redundancy.** *Test:* Cross-knockdown of TUBA1C vs TUBB4B; read Ki-67 and cell-cycle entry. *Prediction:* TUBA1C loss phenocopies loss of the PTMA–Ki-67 coupling only in TUBB4B-low cells (and vice versa) — demonstrating functional substitutability of the two spindle arms.

**H7. Cell-cycle-phase mapping of the two zones.** *Test:* FUCCI-sorted expression profiling + synchronized time-course (PTMA, MKI67, HNRNPA2B1, PABPC1, TUBB4B, TUBA1C). *Prediction:* Zone-14 signature peaks in S/G2–M (TUBB4B-driven), whereas the Zone-22 signature is enriched in late G1/S. Retention of PTMA–Ki-67 coupling in G1/S would support a genuinely **transcriptional/chromatin-level** (not mitotic-accumulation) mechanism for PTMA's effect.

**H8. Subtype/clinical stratification.** *Test:* Cluster METABRIC/TCGA-BRCA by the two zone signatures and test associations with PAM50 subtype, grade, ER status, Ki-67 IHC, and outcome. *Prediction:* Zone-22-like tumors form a translationally skewed, lower-mitotic-load subgroup (plausibly ER+/luminal) that nevertheless shows high Ki-67 and inferior prognosis — and preferential sensitivity to translation-axis inhibitors (e.g., mTOR/4E-pathway inhibitors), consistent with the translational-control model of cancer (Silvera et al. 2010).

---

## Integrated summary

The tree reveals that **PTMA's heavy positive attribution to Ki-67 is a context-conditional, three-module phenomenon**: PTMA (a Myc-responsive acidic histone chaperone) is a faithful proxy of Ki-67 precisely when the tumor simultaneously runs (i) high RNA processing (HNRNPA2B1, PABPC1), (ii) sufficient translation/ribosome output (RPLP0, PABPC1), and (iii) an active spindle program (TUBB4B **or** TUBA1C). Node 14 defines the canonical all-on state (~62% of high-attribution samples, highest purity); Node 22 defines the compensatory state where poly(A)-dependent translation and the α-tubulin arm substitute for TUBB4B. Both zones converge on one mechanistic conclusion: **PTMA and Ki-67 are co-regulated effectors of the Myc/E2F proliferation program, with PTMA providing the chromatin-permissive step (H1 displacement/coactivation) that sustains MKI67 transcription — and the model trusts PTMA only when the supporting RNA/protein/mitotic machinery is engaged.**

---

# Biological Interpretation Report: PTMA→Ki-67 Attribution Logic in Breast Cancer

## 1. Framing: What the Tree is Actually Telling Us

Before diving into the zones, one key clarification on interpretation:

- **Class 1 = the top-decile "Positive Attribution" samples** — i.e., tumors where PTMA's expression *pushed the Ki-67 prediction upward most strongly* in the upstream MLP.
- **The tree splits do not contain PTMA itself** — they are drawn from the other top IG-attributing features. Therefore, the tree describes the *co-expression contexts (the surrounding regulatory network) in which PTMA becomes maximally informative about Ki-67*.
- Because `class_weight = {0:1, 1:4}`, the reported Gini values are class-weighted: Node 14's weighted purity (~81% weighted Class 1) and raw precision (51.4%) against a ~10% class prior represents a **~5.1× enrichment**.
- Thresholds (e.g., 0.333, 0.489, 0.169) are cohort-normalized expression values (z-like), meaning the zones capture **moderately, coordinately elevated** expression across multiple genes — a *program state*, not single-gene extremes.

**Zone ranking by robustness (TP × Precision):**

| Rank | Node | Rule (compact) | TP | Precision | Lift vs. 10% prior | Share of captured Class-1 TP |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **14** | HNRNPA2B1↑ **AND** TUBB4B↑ **AND** RPLP0↑ | **1,147** | **51.4%** | ~5.1× | ~62% |
| **2** | **22** | HNRNPA2B1↑ **AND** TUBB4B↓ **AND** PABPC1↑ **AND** TUBA1C↑ | **268** | **38.8%** | ~3.9× | ~15% |
| 3 | 16 | HNRNPA2B1↓ **AND** RPLP0↑↑ **AND** TUBB4B≳avg **AND** TUBA1C↑ | 189 | 34.9% | ~3.5× | ~10% |
| 4 | 13 | HNRNPA2B1↑ **AND** TUBB4B↑ **AND** RPLP0↓ | 239 | 23.8% | ~2.4× | ~13% |

Two structural observations from the full tree (supplementary): **(a)** every Class-1 leaf requires a spindle gene (TUBB4B or TUBA1C) — high PTMA attribution *never* occurs without mitotic-gene engagement; **(b)** RPL21/RPS27 appear only in Class-0 branches — when the translation/ribosome arm fails, the attribution state collapses. These reinforce the interpretations below.

---

## 2. The Feature Cohort is a Recognized MYC–E2F Proliferation Module

| Feature | Molecular role | "Arm" of the growth program |
|---|---|---|
| HNRNPA2B1 | MYC-regulated splicing factor / m6A-dependent RNA processing | RNA processing (spliceosome) |
| PABPC1 | Poly(A)-binding protein; mRNA stability + translation initiation | mRNA stabilization/translation |
| RPLP0 (36B4), RPL21, RPS27 | Ribosomal stalk/structural proteins | Ribosome biogenesis (nucleolar) |
| TUBB4B, TUBA1C | α/β-tubulin heterodimers (mitotic spindle) | Mitotic commitment (G2/M) |
| **PTMA** | Histone-H1 chaperone, chromatin decondensation; direct MYC target; required for S-phase | Chromatin permissiveness |
| **MKI67 (Ki-67)** | Mitotic perichromosomal-layer protein | Cell-cycle output marker |

---

## 3. HIGHLIGHT ZONE 1 — Node 14 (the dominant, most robust zone)

**Rule:** `HNRNPA2B1 > 0.333 AND TUBB4B > 0.489 AND RPLP0 > 0.169`
**TP = 1,147 | Precision = 51.4% | Weighted Gini purity ≈ 81% | Captures ~62% of all high-attribution samples.**
(Contrast: Node 13, the same zone with `RPLP0 ≤ 0.169`, collapses to 23.8% precision.)

### 3.1 Biological decoding of the rule
This leaf states: *PTMA's positive contribution to Ki-67 prediction is extreme precisely when a tumor simultaneously shows (i) elevated RNA-processing/splicing throughput (HNRNPA2B1), (ii) an activated mitotic spindle gene program (TUBB4B), and (iii) at least baseline-plus ribosomal protein output (RPLP0).* Together with the umbrella rule (HNRNPA2B1↑ + TUBB4B↑ covers Nodes 13+14 = ~75% of captured Class-1 TP), the tree's logic is: **PTMA is most informative about Ki-67 when the cell is deep inside the full MYC–E2F "ribosome + spliceosome + spindle" state.**

The integrative pathway model:

```
Oncogenic drive (MYC amplification/ER-PI3K signaling in breast ca.)
  → MYC induces: PTMA (direct target; evicts linker histone H1 → open chromatin)
                 HNRNPA2B1 (MYC-controlled splicing of growth mRNAs)
                 RPLP0/RPL21/RPS27 + Pol I/III activity (ribosome biogenesis)
                 translation apparatus (incl. PABPC1)
  → MYC → Cyclin D/CDK4 → RB release → E2F
  → E2F induces: TUBB4B/TUBA1C (spindle) + MKI67 (Ki-67)
  → PTMA maintains decondensed chromatin at growth/cell-cycle loci
     → sustains high transcriptional output (incl. MKI67)  [positive reinforcement]
  → Ki-67 protein accumulates through G2/M, where tubulins mark the same phase
```

PTMA thus sits mid-circuit: it is both a **MYC output** and a **facilitator of the program that produces Ki-67**. Two additional properties likely explain why PTMA — rather than a tubulin — carries the heaviest attribution: PTMA is expressed throughout interphase of cycling cells (broad dynamic range, matching Ki-67's own G1–M expression), and its gene is reported to be intronless, making its transcript level a near-direct Pol II readout of MYC activity, insulated from splicing throughput.

### 3.2 Category 1 — Findings that directly confirm existing literature
1. **PTMA is a proliferation-linked oncoprotein**: PTMA expression is induced with proliferation/Transformation (Eschenfeldt & Berger, 1986) and antisense-mediated PTMA depletion arrests proliferation of human tumor cells (Sburlati, Manrow & Berger, 1993). Our in-pipeline PTMA–Ki-67 correlation plus this zone's embedding in a proliferation module directly recapitulates this.
2. **PTMA is a MYC-program member**: PTMA/prothymosin α appears among MYC-regulated genes in systematic MYC target screens (Coller et al., 2000; O'Connell et al., 2003) — consistent with the tree co-selecting canonical MYC targets (ribosomal proteins, hnRNPs) as the context for PTMA attribution.
3. **The tree's hierarchy mirrors MYC→E2F architecture**: MYC controls hnRNP splicing factors and ribosomal protein genes (David et al., 2010; Kim et al., 2000; Arabi et al., 2005; van Riggelen et al., 2010; Dang, 2012); E2F target networks include spindle and chromatin genes (Ren et al., 2002; Bracken et al., 2004). The root-to-leaf ordering (splicing → spindle → ribosome) is a statistical rediscovery of this circuit.
4. **PTMA and Ki-67 are parallel chromatin-level effectors of division**: PTMA binds and displaces linker histone H1, decondensing chromatin during S-phase (Karetsou et al., 2002–2005; Papamarcaki group), while Ki-67 itself forms the perichromosomal layer and functions as a chromatin "surfactant" in mitosis (Schlüter et al., 1993; Cuylen et al., 2016; Sobecki et al., 2017). Co-expression of these two chromatin proteins is therefore expected — and mechanistically meaningful — in dividing cells.
5. **Tubulin/Ki-67 co-expression = mitotic index**, the standard histopathologic coupling exploited by taxane therapy in breast cancer (Jordan & Wilson, 2004; Dowsett et al., 2011; Goldhirsch et al., 2013).

### 3.3 Category 2 — New testable mechanisms
- **H1: PTMA is a functional prerequisite for high MKI67 transcription (chromatin-gate mechanism).** Test: siRNA/CRISPRi of PTMA in MYC-driven breast lines (MDA-MB-231, HCC1937, BT-549; MYC-high) ± synchronized release; quantify MKI67 mRNA (qPCR), Ki-67 protein (flow/IHC), H1 occupancy and accessibility at the MKI67 locus and MYC/E2F target promoters (ATAC-seq, H1 ChIP). Rescue with histone-binding-deficient PTMA mutants to map the chromatin dependency. Expected: PTMA loss lowers MKI67 *before* overt cell-cycle collapse, supporting causality rather than mere co-regulation.
- **H2 (gatekeeper hypothesis, Node 13 vs. 14): the PTMA→Ki-67 signal requires ribosome biogenesis (RPLP0 axis).** Test: attenuate Pol I (low-dose actinomycin D) or knock down RPLP0 and ask whether PTMA overexpression still elevates MKI67; stratify by nucleolar markers (fibrillarin/NPM1). Expected: PTMA's effect on MKI67 is attenuated in low-ribosome contexts — explaining the 23.8% vs 51.4% precision split.
- **H3 (microenvironment noise hypothesis): in RPLP0-low contexts, PTMA signal partly originates from tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes.** PTMA is abundantly expressed in lymphoid/thymic cells (its very name derives from thymosin biology; Haritos et al., 1984). Test: immune deconvolution (CIBERSORT/xCell) of Node 13 vs. Node 14 tumors; predict higher lymphocyte fraction in Node 13. If confirmed, Zone-14-type rules are, in effect, tumor-cell-intrinsic purification criteria.
- **H4: Zone-14 phenotype maps to MYC-active, Ki-67-high breast cancer subtypes** (basal-like/TNBC or luminal B). Test: overlay the rules on TCGA/METABRIC with PAM50 subtyping and MYC activity signatures; correlate with clinical Ki-67 and prognosis. Also test whether a combined PTMA+HNRNPA2B1+TUBB4B+RPLP0 module score outperforms single-gene Ki-67 status as a prognostic/predictive variable.
- **H5 (therapeutic): PTMA knockdown should preferentially impair Zone-14-phenotype tumors and synergize with spindle poisons.** Test: PTMA antisense/siRNA ± paclitaxel/docetaxel in patient-derived organoids stratified by the Zone-14 rule.

---

## 4. HIGHLIGHT ZONE 2 — Node 22 (second-best zone)

**Rule:** `HNRNPA2B1 > 0.333 AND TUBB4B <= 0.489 AND PABPC1 > 0.645 AND TUBA1C > 0.588`
**TP = 268 | Precision = 38.8% | Weighted purity ≈ 72% | ~15% of captured Class-1 TP.**

### 4.1 Biological decoding of the rule
This leaf captures a **conditional-dependency "detour"**: when the canonical β-tubulin arm (TUBB4B) is *not* elevated, PTMA's positive attribution is recovered only if (i) **PABPC1 is high** (mRNA stabilization/poly(A)-driven translation initiation) *and* (ii) **TUBA1C is high** (α-tubulin, an alternative spindle isotype). Notably, the TUBA1C > 0.588 boundary recurs identically in Node 16 — the model re-uses the same mitotic threshold. The interpretation is that the MLP's reliance on PTMA reflects a **generalized "mRNA turnover + mitosis" axis**, in which individual genes are interchangeable surrogates: microtubules are α/β heterodimers, so any engaged isotype reports spindle demand; and post-transcriptional amplification (PABPC1) can compensate when the β-tubulin transcript arm is muted. In other words, **PTMA's attribution to Ki-67 is a property of the program state, not of any single partner gene** — explaining the attribution's robustness across expression configurations (Node 16 provides the third, splicing-low route, again requiring translation↑ + mitotic α-tubulin↑).

### 4.2 Category 1 — Findings that directly confirm existing literature
1. **Tubulin isotype redundancy is real spindle biology** (Cleveland et al., 1980; Jordan & Wilson, 2004): α- and β-tubulins co-assemble as heterodimers, so TUBA1C-high can report functional spindle output even when one β isotype is low — exactly what the tree's OR-like logic encodes.
2. **PABPC1 is the master mRNA-stabilizing/translation-initiation scaffold** needed for the short-lived, high-turnover proliferation transcriptome (Gray et al., 2000; Hershey, Sonenberg & Mathews, 2012) — its requirement here confirms that the post-transcriptional arm of the growth program is engaged.
3. **Splicing/translation-factor engagement alongside PTMA is MYC-consistent**: MYC simultaneously drives hnRNPs, translation machinery, and metabolic isoform switches (David et al., 2010; Alarcón et al., 2015; Dang, 2012). Node 22 = the RNA-processing arm high (HNRNPA2B1↑) plus a translation arm high (PABPC1↑) — two arms of the same MYC output replacing the missing β-tubulin readout while TUBA1C keeps the mitotic readout.
4. **Ki-67/tubulin co-expression as cell-cycle phase readout** (Gerdes et al., 1983; Whitfield et al., 2002): tubulins and MKI67 are periodically expressed genes; the requirement of *some* spindle gene in every Class-1 leaf matches the known G2/M co-expression of MKI67 and spindle components.

### 4.3 Category 2 — New testable mechanisms
- **H6 (PABPC1-dependent stabilization route): in TUBB4B-low tumors, MKI67 mRNA maintenance depends on PABPC1.** Test: PABPC1 knockdown in TUBB4B-low/PTMA-high lines (e.g., selected breast models); measure MKI67 mRNA half-life (actinomycin D chase), polysome loading (ribosome profiling), and PABPC1-bound poly(A)+ transcripts (RIP-seq). Expected: MKI67 falls specifically when the PABPC1 arm is removed — establishing a post-transcriptional mechanism for maintaining high Ki-67 output.
- **H7 (isotype substitution): Zone-2 tumors express alternative β-isotypes (TUBB2A/B, TUBB) that partner with TUBA1C.** Test: expression analysis of all β-tubulin genes in Node-22 tumors; CRISPR single knockouts of TUBB4B with rescue by alternative isotypes in spindle-assembly assays. Expected: functional compensation, confirming the model reads the module, not the gene.
- **H8 (state distinction): Zone 2 may mark a translation-dominant/earlier cell-cycle state (G1/S–biased) versus the G2/M-dominant Zone 1.** Test: cell-cycle phase scoring (Whitfield periodic gene sets, FUCCI-like signatures) across the two zones; pathway activity inference (mTORC1/eIF4F, E2F, MYC). Prediction: Zone 2 = higher mTOR/translation, lower mitotic index — with equivalent Ki-67 output maintained via mRNA stabilization.
- **H9 (clinical corollary):** If Zone-2 tumors are spindle-program-poor by transcript (despite TUBA1C↑), taxane sensitivity may differ from Zone-1 tumors — testable in expression/response datasets and organoid drug screens.

## 5. Integrated Synthesis — Why PTMA Carries the Heaviest Attribution for Ki-67

The tree, read biologically, states that **PTMA is the highest-information continuous readout of the MYC–E2F chromatin–biosynthesis–mitosis circuit that produces Ki-67**:

1. **Shared transcriptional driver:** PTMA is a MYC target; MKI67/spindle genes are E2F/MYC-driven; ribosomal and hnRNP genes are MYC outputs. In samples where the full module is on (Zone 1), PTMA level ≈ MYC activity ≈ proliferative state ≈ Ki-67 — hence extreme positive IG attribution.
2. **Functional (not just correlative) coupling:** PTMA's H1-chaperone activity keeps growth loci accessible and is required for S-phase progression; Ki-67 is the mitotic-chromatin downstream marker. PTMA is effectively the *chromatin arm* of the program whose output is measured as Ki-67.
3. **Temporal coverage advantage:** PTMA (interphase-graded) co-varies with Ki-67 (G1–M) more smoothly than M-phase-restricted tubulins — the MLP exploits this.
4. **Conditional dependency:** PTMA's signal is only reliable when biosynthetic (RPLP0) and mitotic (TUBB4B/TUBA1C) arms confirm tumor-cell commitment; otherwise PTMA signal decouples (Node 13's precision collapse; lymphocyte-source noise hypothesis).
5. **Redundant readout architecture** (Zone 2 + Node 16): splicing-arm, translation-arm, and either tubulin isotype can substitute for one another — the attribution state is a *program property*, which is why it generalizes.

**Priority experiments:** (1) PTMA knockdown → MKI67/ATAC-seq causality test (H1); (2) RPLP0/Pol I gatekeeping test (H2) + immune deconvolution of Node 13 vs. 14 (H3); (3) subtype/TCGA-METABRIC mapping of Zone 14 (H4); (4) PABPC1–MKI67 mRNA half-life test in Zone 2 (H6); (5) PTMA-ASO/taxane synergy screen (H5/H9).

**Caveats:** IG attribution identifies *informational dependence*, not causation — the hypotheses above convert it to causal tests; Class-1 labels derive from the extreme 10% under positive-attribution analysis with 4:1 class weighting, which favors recall; thresholds are cohort-normalized and dataset-specific.

# Biological Interpretation: PTMA → Ki-67 Decision-Tree Logic in Breast Cancer

## 1. Quantitative frame and zone ranking

Class 1 = top 10% of samples by positive IG attribution of PTMA, so the base prevalence is ~10%. Any leaf precision above 10% therefore represents enrichment of the high-attribution state:

| Rank | Node | TP | FP | Precision | Enrichment | Share of all Class-1 samples |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **14** | **1147** | 1086 | **51.4%** | ~5.1× | ~62% |
| **2** | **22** | **268** | 423 | **38.8%** | ~3.9× | ~15% |
| 3 | 16 | 189 | 352 | 34.9% | ~3.5× | ~10% |
| 4 | 13 | 239 | 765 | 23.8% | ~2.4× | ~13% |

**Node 14 is the primary (most robust) zone** — it holds >half of all high-attribution samples and the lowest Gini (0.31). **Node 22 is the second zone** by both TP and precision. Nodes 13 and 16 are treated as built-in contrasts, not as primary evidence.

**Overall tree architecture.** The tree encodes a three-module gating system, with the root split always at the same module:

- **Module A — RNA processing gate:** HNRNPA2B1 (pre-mRNA splicing/processing/handling of cell-cycle transcripts)
- **Module B — Translation gate:** RPLP0 (ribosome stalk / ribosome output) or PABPC1 (poly(A)-tail stabilization + closed-loop initiation)
- **Module C — Mitotic spindle gate:** TUBB4B (βIVb-tubulin) or TUBA1C (α1c-tubulin)

The central biological claim: **PTMA only carries strong positive information about Ki-67 when the full proliferation program — RNA processing + protein synthesis + spindle commitment — is simultaneously engaged.** In that state, PTMA and MKI67 are two co-regulated arms of the same c-Myc/E2F cell-cycle circuit (PTMA = chromatin/S-phase executor; Ki-67 = mitotic executor), so the nonlinear model leans on PTMA maximally. Outside that state, PTMA expression fluctuates for reasons unrelated to division (stress, immune/extracellular roles, background noise), which dilutes the global PTMA–Ki-67 correlation and explains why Integrated Gradients concentrates attribution in these zones.

## 2. ZONE 1 (PRIMARY): Node 14 — `HNRNPA2B1 > 0.333 AND TUBB4B > 0.489 AND RPLP0 > 0.169`

### 2.1 Translation of the rule into biology
This is a **triple-positive proliferative state**:
- **HNRNPA2B1 high** → transcriptionally hyperactive cell under heavy pre-mRNA processing/splicing load (oncogenic RBP; spliceosome-dependent maturation of cell-cycle transcripts).
- **TUBB4B high** → mitotic spindle β-tubulin isotype elevated; cells have built M-phase machinery.
- **RPLP0 > 0.169** → ribosomal stalk protein P0 (36B4) above population mean; ribosome output sufficient to sustain protein synthesis (classical Myc ribosome program).

### 2.2 Mechanistic rationale: why PTMA's attribution peaks here
PTMA (prothymosin α) is a ~11 kDa, highly acidic, intrinsically disordered **nuclear histone chaperone** and **transcriptional co-activator**, a **direct c-Myc target gene**, whose expression tracks growth fraction, is overexpressed in carcinomas, and is a **common-essential proliferation gene in genome-wide CRISPR screens (DepMap)**. Ki-67 is the nuclear/mitotic-phase marker of the same program (perichromosomal layer; mitotic chromosome dispersion). Because c-Myc simultaneously drives PTMA, ribosomal proteins (RPLP0), translation factors, and RNA-processing demand, while E2F/cell-cycle machinery drives MKI67 and tubulins, **the triple-positive background certifies that a PTMA signal is genuinely "cycling cell" and not noise** — hence maximal, positive, PTMA→Ki-67 attribution.

### 2.3 The built-in contrast (Node 13): RPLP0 is the "gain control"
Nodes 13/14 differ **only** at RPLP0. Dropping RPLP0 ≤ 0.169 halves precision (23.8%) and pushes Gini to ~0.49 (maximal uncertainty). Interpretation: high splicing + high spindle machinery **without ribosomal output** does not reliably co-occur with high PTMA attribution. Biologically: (i) insufficient ribosome biogenesis engages the **ribosomal-protein/p53 nucleolar-stress checkpoint** that brakes proliferation regardless of PTMA transcripts; and/or (ii) PTMA and Ki-67 are both **short-lived, high-turnover proteins** that cannot be maintained without translation capacity, so protein-level coupling fails; and/or (iii) RPLP0-low cells may express tubulin/splicing genes for non-mitotic remodeling (stress/differentiation), a state where PTMA says nothing about Ki-67.

### 2.4 Findings that directly confirm literature knowledge
1. **PTMA is a proliferation-tied, Myc-inducible nuclear protein** — its attribution concentrates exclusively in cycling-state backgrounds (Guo et al. 2000; Coller et al. 2000; Menssen & Hermeking 2002; DepMap/Behan et al. 2019).
2. **Ki-67 co-activates with mitotic machinery** (spindle tubulins) exactly as described from G1–M-phase expression and its mitotic chromosome function (Gerdes et al. 1983, 1984; Cuylen et al. 2016; Sun & Kaufman 2018).
3. **Myc's tripartite transcriptional output — RNA processing, ribosome biogenesis, cell-cycle/spindle genes — is retrieved as the exact zone composition** (Coller et al. 2000; Guo et al. 2000).
4. **hnRNP A2/B1 elevation as a proliferative epithelial-tumor marker** (He & Smith 2009; hnRNP A2/B1 early lung-carcinogenesis detection work, Tockman et al. 1997 [verify]).
5. **Ki-67 as the clinical proliferation standard in breast cancer** (Yerushalmi et al. 2010) is consistent with the model requiring PTMA's strongest attribution in actively cycling breast tumor cells.

### 2.5 New testable mechanisms (hypotheses)
- **H1 — Translation-gating hypothesis:** PTMA→Ki-67 coupling requires ribosome output. *Prediction:* in TCGA-BRCA/METABRIC, PTMA–MKI67 correlation and IG-attribution strength persist only in RPLP0-high strata. *Experiment:* RPLP0 siRNA or Pol I inhibition (CX-5461) in MCF-7/T47D/MDA-MB-231 → measure MKI67 mRNA/protein, Ki-67⁺ fraction (flow/IF), and PTMA protein; expect decoupling.
- **H2 — RP-stress/p53-dependence hypothesis:** the RPLP0 gate exists because ribosome insufficiency triggers the RP–p53 checkpoint that PTMA's pro-survival activity cannot fully buffer. *Experiment:* repeat H1 in TP53-WT (MCF-7) vs TP53-mutant (MDA-MB-231/BT-549) lines; predict stronger decoupling in TP53-WT. Support: Zhang & Lu 2009.
- **H3 — hnRNP A2/B1-dependent processing of MKI67/PTMA transcripts:** eCLIP/RIP-qPCR for HNRNPA2B1 on PTMA and MKI67 pre-mRNAs; knockdown → isoform usage, mRNA half-life, Ki-67⁺ fraction.
- **H4 — PTMA–Ki-67 chromatin/mitotic axis:** PTMA knockdown should impair Ki-67 perichromosomal localization and mitotic progression (chromosome spreads, live-cell imaging), rescueable by WT but not acidic-domain-mutant PTMA. Support: PTMA histone/CBP co-activator literature (Karetsou et al.); Cuylen et al. 2016.
- **H5 — Feed-forward loop:** PTMA as co-activator amplifies the Myc program itself (Module B/C genes). PTMA overexpression/knockdown → PRO-seq/ChIP-qPCR of Myc targets.

## 3. ZONE 2 (SECONDARY): Node 22 — `HNRNPA2B1 > 0.333 AND TUBB4B <= 0.489 AND PABPC1 > 0.645 AND TUBA1C > 0.588`

### 3.1 Translation of the rule into biology
Same **Module A gate** (HNRNPA2B1 high; internal replication of Zone 1's root condition = robustness check), but with **two substitution rules**:
- **TUBB4B NOT elevated, yet TUBA1C high** → the mitotic module is satisfied by an α-tubulin isotype instead of βIVb-tubulin → **microtubule isotype redundancy**.
- **RPLP0 not required here; PABPC1 high instead** → the translation module is satisfied by **mRNA stabilization/closed-loop initiation** (poly(A)-binding protein) rather than ribosome-stalk expansion.

Per the raw tree, both substitutions are **jointly necessary**: sibling leaves with PABPC1 ≤ 0.645, or with TUBA1C ≤ 0.588, fall to Class 0. The high-attribution state is therefore defined by **functional module states, not by specific gene products**.

### 3.2 Mechanistic rationale
In this subpopulation, spindle competence is achieved with an α-tubulin-dominant program, and translational drive comes from mRNA stabilization/efficient initiation (PABPC1) — plausibly stabilizing and efficiently translating PTMA and MKI67 poly(A)⁺ transcripts. PTMA–Ki-67 coupling survives because the *functional states* (RNA handling, translation efficiency, spindle assembly) — not individual transcripts — define the cycling attractor. This mirrors known tubulin-isotype heterogeneity across tumors (isotype switching is well documented, including in taxane resistance) and PABP's role in sustaining growth-dependent translation.

### 3.3 Findings that directly confirm literature knowledge
1. **The HNRNPA2B1 RNA-processing gate replicates in an independent branch** — robust confirmation of the primary gate (He & Smith 2009; Tockman et al. [verify]).
2. **Microtubule isotype flexibility in cancer**: tumors differ in β/α-tubulin isotype expression, with functionally interchangeable contributions to the spindle (Leandro-García et al. 2010; Kavallaris, Nat Rev Cancer 2010; Dumontet & Jordan 2010).
3. **PABPC1's closed-loop/poly(A) function as a growth-coupled translation mechanism** (Kahvejian et al. 2005).
4. **Cell-cycle-regulated expression of α-tubulin genes and their elevation in proliferating tumors** (Leandro-García et al. 2010; recent pan-cancer reports on TUBA1C [verify]).

### 3.4 New testable mechanisms (hypotheses)
- **H6 — Isotype-substitution (functional spindle-state) hypothesis:** within TUBB4B-low tumors, PTMA–MKI67 coupling persists only if TUBA1C is high. *Experiment:* cohort stratification as above; in vitro TUBB4B knockdown ± TUBA1C rescue → spindle IF (cold-stable microtubules), mitotic transit, MKI67/PTMA readout.
- **H7 — PABPC1 mRNA-stabilization hypothesis:** PABPC1 directly stabilizes/translationally boosts MKI67 and PTMA transcripts in this subpopulation. *Experiment:* PABPC1 knockdown + actinomycin D chase (mRNA half-life), TAIL-seq (poly(A) tails), 3′UTR luciferase reporters, ribosome profiling (translation efficiency). *Prediction:* Zone-2-like cells regulate PTMA/Ki-67 post-transcriptionally, unlike the ribosome-output-driven Zone-1 configuration.
- **H8 — Two alternative routes to the same proliferative attractor** (biogenesis-driven vs mRNA-stability-driven) → **subtype-specific vulnerabilities**: Zone-1-like tumors → Pol I/ribosome-targeting (CX-5461); Zone-2-like tumors → translation-initiation/PABP-interaction or NMD-axis targeting. Test with matched viability/PRO-seq assays.
- **H9 — Clinical translation:** the Zone-2 signature (HNRNPA2B1-high/PABPC1-high/TUBA1C-high, TUBB4B-low) marks spindle-dominant dependence; *prediction:* preferential taxane response in neoadjuvant paclitaxel transcriptomic cohorts (public GEO/EBI datasets), with PTMA adding predictive value beyond Ki-67 alone.
- *(Exploratory)* HNRNPA2B1's reported role in RNA/miRNA sorting into exosomes (Villarroya-Beltri et al. [verify]) could link Zone-2 tumors to altered EV-RNA content — worth screening but low priority for the Ki-67 axis.

## 4. Integrated model (supplementary context from the full tree)

Supplementary leaves reinforce modular redundancy rather than contradict it: **Node 16** (HNRNPA2B1-low, RPLP0 > 0.444, TUBB4B above threshold, TUBA1C > 0.588) shows that when the RNA-processing gate fails, *stronger* translation plus *both* tubulin isotypes can partially compensate (~3.5× enrichment) — a hierarchy A → B/C with deep redundancy. **Node 13** serves as the negative control proving RPLP0's gating role. Net model:

> **PTMA is the chromatin-executor node of the c-Myc/E2F proliferation circuit; Ki-67 is its mitotic-executor readout. PTMA carries predictive information about Ki-67 only when the full three-module program (RNA processing [HNRNPA2B1] ∧ translation [RPLP0 or PABPC1] ∧ spindle [TUBB4B or TUBA1C]) is engaged.** The two highlighted zones are two alternative, factor-flexible configurations of the same attractor.

## 5. Caveats and validation checklist
- Thresholds are in normalized (z-score-like) units; leaves are optimized for Class-1 recall (class weight 0:1/1:4), so interpret precision as **enrichment (~5×/4×), not diagnostic accuracy**.
- Findings are correlative and model-derived (IG labels). Priority validation: (1) stratified PTMA–MKI67 correlation in TCGA-BRCA/METABRIC per zone logic; (2) perturbation experiments H1–H7 in luminal and triple-negative breast cancer lines; (3) H9 clinical pharmacotranscriptomic testing.
